title: Evaluation of care in hospitalised geriatric patients with rheumatic diseases
summary:
Increasing age, frailty, impaired mobility and other age-related factors may make regular rheumatological care more difficult. The RHEUM-HELD study therefore aims to investigate the rheumatological care of older patients with rheumatic diseases who require inpatient geriatric treatment.

Rheumatological care in hospitalised geriatric patients will be compared with that of similarly aged patients receiving outpatient rheumatological care. The study assesses, among other factors, antirheumatic medication, regular care by a rheumatologist and the activity of the underlying rheumatic disease.

In a prospective part of the study, handgrip strength and hand function are additionally assessed. Hospitalised geriatric patients with rheumatic diseases are compared with rheumatology outpatients and older hospitalised oncology patients. No study-specific pharmacological or therapeutic intervention is performed.

interventions.name: Patients aged 60 or older with an underlying rheumatic disease who received inpatient geriatric care in 2021, 2022, or 2023. Retrospective collection of demographic and geriatric parameters, information on the underlying rheumatic disease, medication therapy, and rheumatologic care.
Patients aged 60 or older with an underlying rheumatic condition from the rheumatology outpatient clinic, serving as a comparison group for the inpatient geriatric cohort.

100 inpatients aged 60 or older receiving geriatric care and diagnosed with an underlying rheumatic disease. Collection of clinical, geriatric, and rheumatological parameters, as well as a one-time assessment of hand strength and hand function.

100 outpatients receiving rheumatology treatment who were of comparable age and had comparable disease activity. Collection of clinical and rheumatological parameters, as well as a one-time assessment of hand strength and hand function.

100 inpatients receiving geriatric treatment who were of comparable age and frailty status and had no underlying rheumatic disease. Collection of clinical and geriatric parameters, as well as a one-time assessment of hand strength and hand function.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For the rheumatology study groups:
Age ≥ 60 years.
Confirmed underlying inflammatory rheumatic disease.
Inpatient treatment in geriatrics or outpatient rheumatology treatment.
For the prospective study arm: sufficient knowledge of German and sufficient cognitive ability to understand the study information and the informed consent form.
For the group without an underlying inflammatory rheumatic disease:
Age ≥ 60 years.
Inpatient treatment in geriatrics.
No underlying rheumatic disease.
For the prospective study phase, sufficient knowledge of German and sufficient cognitive ability to understand the study information and the informed consent form.
Exclusion criteria:
None
